structured_output.name: CareFall
structured_output.tagline: Fall-detection device on an ESP8266 that pushes alerts to a Firebase-backed web app.
structured_output.description:
CareFall is an IoT project for fall detection. I built the firmware for an ESP8266 board with an MPU6050 motion sensor, plus an installable web app for managing devices and receiving alerts. When the device detects a fall, it switches on an LED and a buzzer. The wearer can silence it with a physical button.

On the hardware side, I wrote the Arduino C++ firmware. It reads the MPU6050 on all three axes, turns the readings into a single score and compares it to a threshold that is easy to change. It connects over WiFi to a Firebase Realtime Database. It reads a per-device notification delay from the database and, once that delay has passed without the alarm being cleared, writes a fall flag back. Pressing the button clears the alarm locally and resets the flag in the database.

The front end is a progressive web app in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, using the Firebase JavaScript SDK. It has a manifest and a service worker so it can be installed and show system notifications. The app lists registered devices with a status indicator. I added pages to register a device by its code and name, rename it, set the notification delay from 0 to 60 seconds, switch it active or inactive, and remove it. The pages poll the database and raise a notification when a fall is flagged on an active device. What I would highlight is that it connects embedded hardware, a cloud database and an installable app into one working loop.
